summary: Redwood team walked Cloudwave through the Console usage analytics and per-route dashboards with a focus on cost breakdown and optimization (batching, caching, quantization). Customer liked the per-route cost drilldown and asked about data residency, SOC2, and benchmark methodology. Agreed next steps to start a POC and share pricing/security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Ava from Redwood, joined by Rohan (our SE) and Lina from product. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Daniel Kim: Good, thanks. Excited to see the console walkthrough — we're evaluating infra and cost for embedding generation across services.
[00:15] Sara Ortiz: Quick note, we've got Tom and Priya on for security and infra questions.
[00:21] Ava Martinez: Great. We'll go through the Console — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, and then leave time for technical Q&A. Roughly 30-40 minutes. Sound good?
[00:30] Tom Liu: Yep.
[00:32] Rohan Gupta: I'll start with the UI first, show the per-route tables and then dig into the cost model and how batching/caching changes things.
[00:40] [screen share starts] Rohan Gupta: So this is the main dashboard — top-level token volume and spend by model. You can filter by date range, project, and route.
[00:50] Rohan Gupta: Notice the spikes here, those are from our prefix-caching hits which reduces repeated token generation costs. We expose cache hit rates at the route level.
[01:05] Priya Rao: Can you show an example route? We have 150 routes across product and infra.
[01:12] Rohan Gupta: Sure — here's the search-suggestions route. On the right is a cost breakdown: model cost, infra (GPU time), and overhead. The unit cost is broken down per 1k tokens and per inference call.
[01:28] Daniel Kim: That per-route breakdown is really helpful. Our current billing is more coarse, so we can't tell which route is driving embeddings cost.
[01:35] Rohan Gupta: Exactly — and you can set alerts per-route for spend or latency.
[01:42] Sara Ortiz: How accurate is the cost estimate vs actual invoice?
[01:47] Rohan Gupta: We calculate cost from token counts and the model profile (which encodes throughput and ops). For hosted customers we show an estimated bill; for Dedicated we map to reserved capacity units which smooths per-token variance. It's usually within 3-7% of final invoice, depending on batching and KV cache behavior.
[02:05] Tom Liu: What about shared vs dedicated capacity — how do fallbacks work if we hit capacity?
[02:12] Lina Park: You can configure routing policies — prioritize low-latency dedicated pools, fall back to hosted or cheaper quantized variants if capacity constrained. We surfaced that here in the route policy view.
[02:26] Priya Rao: Are there per-region residency options? We need EU data residency for some customers.
[02:32] Ava Martinez: Yes, we support region pinning and Private VPC deployments for strict residency. We also integrate with KMS for key management.
[02:41] Daniel Kim: On security: do you have SOC 2 and audit logging? Our security team insists on SOC 2 and SAML SSO.
[02:47] Rohan Gupta: We are SOC 2 compliant and provide audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC. For Private deployments we can do HSM/KMS integrations. I'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:59] Sara Ortiz: Please do. Also, how do you handle PII in logs — retention policy?
[03:06] Rohan Gupta: Retention is configurable per project; you can opt out of storing request content and keep only metadata.
[03:14] Daniel Kim: Can you show an example of the per-route latency distribution?
[03:18] Rohan Gupta: Sure — here's the percentile chart. You can pivot by model and by request size. See how p95 jumps with sequences >1k tokens — that's where batching behavior changes.
[03:34] Tom Liu: That makes sense. For our use case, most requests are short but we have a heavy tail of long docs.
[03:41] Rohan Gupta: In that case, we recommend hybrid routing: short requests go to low-latency hosted models, long ones to cheaper quantized variants on dedicated pools. The console shows simulated cost impact for changes.
[03:55] Priya Rao: Speaking of quantization, how much does it affect quality for embeddings vs chat?
[04:01] Lina Park: Embeddings often tolerate more aggressive quantization with minimal quality drop — we provide model/quantization recommendations per workload in Optimize. Chat is more sensitive, we recommend eval-based rollouts and A/B testing.
[04:16] Daniel Kim: Can we run a quick simulated POC cost estimation? We have sample traffic for embedding generation of about 50M tokens/month.
[04:24] Rohan Gupta: Yes — upload your sample or share metrics. We can run the benchmark template to show per-route cost and throughput. I'll share the template after.
[04:33] [15:00 mark - mid call discussion summary] Ava Martinez: Quick recap — console shows per-route cost, latency, cache hit rates; routing policies and optimize recs can reduce spend. Next we'll drill into audit logs and POC.
[04:45] Tom Liu: On the POC, how long does it take to get Dedicated capacity reserved?
[04:49] Ava Martinez: Typically 2-4 weeks for reserved Dedicated depending on size; for POC you can start with hosted or short-term dedicated commit.
[04:58] Sara Ortiz: Any hidden fees or network egress charges we should know about?
[05:03] Rohan Gupta: Network egress is billed at cost and visible on the invoice; we show a line-item for infra/network in the cost breakdown.
[05:10] Daniel Kim: Competitor question — how's Redwood different vs Anthropic or Vertex for our use case?
[05:15] Ava Martinez: Two things: production-first controls (per-route cost SLOs, rollouts, explicit caching) and flexibility to run the same runtime hosted, dedicated, or in your VPC. Also, transparent per-token unit economics in the Console.
[05:31] Priya Rao: For the simulated estimate, do you account for batching improvements over time?
[05:36] Rohan Gupta: Yes, the benchmark template models batching and cache hit rates; you can tweak parameters like average request size, concurrency, and cache reuse.
[05:45] [10:00 into call - deeper technical Q&A] Daniel Kim: Our concurrency patterns are bursty — 2k qps sustained for minutes. How do you autoscale without blowing budget?
[05:56] Rohan Gupta: We have autoscaling policies with burst capacity and scheduled scale. For Dedicated you reserve baseline capacity for steady-state and allow controlled burst to hosted or spot pools with fallback policies. The Console exposes cost impact of those policies so you can dial trade-offs.
[06:16] Tom Liu: Do you offer preemptible GPU usage for cost savings?
[06:20] Lina Park: For Dedicated we offer burst on lower-cost instances in certain regions; it's configurable.
[06:26] Sara Ortiz: Is there a way to export the per-route data to our BI stack?
[06:30] Rohan Gupta: Yes — CSV/JSON exports and a query API. We can also push metrics to Datadog/Prometheus.
[06:39] Daniel Kim: Can you show the cost breakdown for a sample route?
[06:42] Rohan Gupta: Here — model compute is 60%, infra overhead 25%, cache saves ~15% in this route. The console shows projected savings from increasing cache TTL from 30s to 5m.
[06:58] Priya Rao: Any caveats on cache consistency or staleness for suggestions?
[07:03] Rohan Gupta: It's configurable by route; we recommend conservative TTLs for critical user-facing content. You can also mark routes as no-cache.
[07:11] [20:00 mark - security deep dive] Tom Liu: For Private deployments, how do upgrades work? We have strict maintenance windows.
[07:18] Lina Park: We support controlled rollouts and can schedule upgrades during your windows, and for air-gapped setups we provide offline packages.
[07:26] Priya Rao: For audit purposes, can we retain raw request logs behind our KMS?
[07:32] Rohan Gupta: Yes, Private customers can keep logs under their KMS/HSM control and we support configurable retention.
[07:38] Daniel Kim: Ok great. After the security packet, our team will review and give feedback.
[07:43] Ava Martinez: Perfect, we'll include SOC 2 cert, pen test summary, and data residency docs.
[07:50] [30:00 mark - closing and next steps] Rohan Gupta: Final note on the Console: the per-route simulated changes let you run 'what-if' scenarios — change batching/concurrency/quantization and get a projected cost delta.
[07:59] Daniel Kim: That 'what-if' tool is actually very helpful. We'll definitely use that in the POC.
[08:04] Ava Martinez: Recap of next steps: we'll send pricing, security pack, benchmark template, and propose POC dates. Any final Qs?
[08:12] Tom Liu: None from me.
[08:14] Sara Ortiz: All good.
[08:16] Priya Rao: Thanks, looks good.
[08:18] Ava Martinez: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email.
[08:22] [call ends]
